::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[In what directory should I store my new LaTeX template?](https://tex.stackexchange.com/questions/262242/in-what-directory-should-i-store-my-new-latex-template), asked by [abcd](https://tex.stackexchange.com/users/85086/abcd) on TeX Stack Exchange (2015-08-19; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> I just downloaded the [elsarticle](http://www.latextemplates.com/template/elseviers-elsarticle-document-class) document class.  In the unzipped directory, there are `.bst` files, `.tex` files, a `.sty` file, a `.pdf` file, and a very unhelpful `README`.
>
> Where should I put these files in order to use them system-wide in my documents?
>
> In reading a [very similar post](https://tex.stackexchange.com/q/10498/85086), I've realized that which version of LaTeX I'm using (one of which is apparently MiKTeX) is relevant here.  How do I figure out what I'm using?  I create LaTeX documents in Emacs, and use `C-c c` to generate PDFs from my `.tex` files.
>
> In reading an [answer to another similar post](https://tex.stackexchange.com/a/1138/85086), I see that I should put my files in the directory returned by
>
> ```latex
> kpsewhich -var-value=TEXMFHOME
> ```
>
> For me, this returns
>
> ```latex
> /home/daniel/texmf
> ```
>
> a directory which *does not exist on my computer*.  What's the deal?
:::

Each distribution should have a local `texmf` directory. Within that, use the [TeX Directory Structure](http://tug.ctan.org/tds/tds.html): 

* `.cls` files go in `tex/latex/elsarticle`
* `.bst` files go in `bibtex/bst/elsarticle`
* the README and `.pdf` go in `doc/elsarticle`

Templates aren't a special kind of file; they are just sample documents to fill in. Some TeX IDE's have a place to put them. For instance in TeXShop they can be put in `/Library/TeXShop/Templates`.  The TDS specifications suggest they can go in `/doc/elsarticle`.
